name: MCP3421 18-bit ADC (I2C)
description: Microchip 18-bit delta-sigma analog-to-digital converter with one differential input (V+ minus V-, ±2.048 V full scale, PGA x1/x2/x4/x8), on-board 2.048 V reference and an I2C interface; 12/14/16/18-bit at 240/60/15/3.75 samples per second. Runs on 2.7-5.5 V. Sold as: Adafruit MCP3421 18-Bit ADC - STEMMA QT / Qwiic (product 5870), 6-pin header VIN, GND, SCL, SDA, V+, V- (V+/V- also on a 2-way screw terminal), 10 kΩ I2C pull-ups, fixed I2C address 0x68.
eli5: Measures one small voltage (even a negative difference between two wires) extremely precisely and sends the number over I2C.

pins.name: VIN
pins.description: Supply, 2.7-5.5 V straight to the chip (no regulator); use the same voltage as your microcontroller's logic (3.3 V for ESP32/Pico). The 10 kΩ SDA/SCL pull-ups go to this pin

pins.name: GND
pins.description: Ground for power, logic and the analog inputs

pins.name: SCL
pins.description: I2C clock (10 kΩ pull-up to VIN on the board)

pins.name: SDA
pins.description: I2C data (10 kΩ pull-up to VIN on the board)

pins.name: V+
pins.description: Positive analog input (VIN+); reading is V+ minus V-, ±2.048 V at gain 1; keep it between GND and VIN (Adafruit advises keeping both inputs within 0-2.048 V)

pins.name: V-
pins.description: Negative analog input (VIN-); tie to GND for single-ended use; keep it between GND and VIN (Adafruit advises keeping both inputs within 0-2.048 V)

buildNotes: VIN feeds the chip directly (no regulator) and the 10 kΩ SDA/SCL pull-ups go to VIN: power it from 3.3 V with an ESP32 or Pico.
The reading is V+ minus V-. For a single-ended voltage tie V- to GND; you then get 0 to +2.048 V at gain 1. Divide larger voltages down first; each input must stay within GND - 0.3 V and VIN + 0.3 V.

One-shot conversion: write one configuration byte 0x80 | rate << 2 | gain (0x8C = 18-bit, gain 1), wait about 267 ms at 18 bits, read 3 data bytes + config byte (2 + 1 below 18 bits) and accept it when bit 7 (RDY) of the config byte is 0.

Volts = code x 2.048 V / 2^(N-1) / PGA: 15.625 µV per code at 18 bits, 62.5 µV at 16 bits, 250 µV at 14 bits, 1 mV at 12 bits (gain 1). Codes are two's complement and saturate instead of rolling over.
The address is fixed at 0x68 (MCP3421A0); use an I2C multiplexer for more than one board.
The V+/V- header pins and the screw terminal are the same two nets: use one or the other.

example.code:
from machine import I2C, Pin
import time
from mcp3421 import MCP3421

i2c = I2C({I2C_ID}, sda=Pin({SDA}), scl=Pin({SCL}), freq=100000)
adc = MCP3421(i2c, addr=0x68, bits=18, gain=1)
while True:
    raw = adc.read_raw()
    print('ADC=%d %.5fV' % (raw, raw * adc.lsb()))
    time.sleep(1)
